_comment: Tracks the full-set examiner pass over BLB (274 cards), goal: every card gets 1-3 examiner/parser-fix iterations, stopping early on a full match or when the remaining gap needs a design decision; non-success cards are left as-is for the user. status: 'match' (full reconstruction confirmed correct -- ALSO added to blb-success.json, which drives app/lib/forgeTranslate.blb.test.ts's snapshot suite) | 'issues-fixed' (a real bug was found+fixed but the card still has an unrelated unfixed gap, so NOT a full match) | 'issues-open' (real gap identified, not fixed -- either narrower than worth a fix pass, or blocked on a bigger schema change) | 'skipped-attempts' (3 examiner loops used, still issues) | 'skipped-rework' (needs a design decision, see note). attempts counts examiner agent runs used (a fix verified by direct node inspection instead of a fresh agent run, to save budget, still counts as using that attempt's slot).
_strategy: Batch 1 (5 cards, full blind examiner each) showed exhaustive per-card examining doesn't scale (~400k+ tokens for 5 cards). Switched to audit-first triage starting batch 2: a static risk-pattern scan (scripts under the job scratch dir, not checked into the repo) flags cards using fragile Forge field shapes; cards hitting only ALREADY-FIXED shared-logic patterns are not re-examined individually (the fix applies uniformly to every card using that pattern); a small diverse spot-check sample is examined per round instead to catch NEW bug classes, and known architectural gaps (see known_gap_classes) are recorded once and applied to every card in that class without spending agent budget on each.

ConditionCheckSVar/ConditionSVarCompare/.description: Forge's system for conditional effects gated on a dynamically-computed value -- cross-player count comparisons (ConditionCheckSVar$/ConditionSVarCompare$, e.g. 'if an opponent controls more lands than you') AND single-player dynamic checks on a STATIC ability (CheckSVar$, e.g. Essence Channeler's 'as long as you've lost life this turn'). Zero translator support for either -- conditions are silently dropped, producing an unconditional effect/ability. A whole unsupported class, not a quick fix -- needs a design decision (a sensor-role extension, or a new cond: convention) before implementing. Flagged for the user. (A narrower, single-object property check on an earlier target -- ConditionDefined$Targeted + ConditionPresent$ Type.powerLEN, or a boolean ConditionPresent$...PromisedGift check -- is NOT in this class; both were cheap enough to implement directly, see Driftgloom Coyote's if_targeted_* flag and Crumb and Get It's/Dawn's Truce's cond:gift_promised.)

Delayed conditional return (DelayedTrigg.description: The real mechanic behind Parting Gust/Salvation Swan's own exile-then-conditionally-return effects: a DelayedTrigger (fires at a future phase) gated by its own ConditionPresent$/ConditionCompare$, returning the object under its OWNER's control (not the caster's) with a counter added. DelayedTrigger's Execute$ child is correctly suppressed now (no longer produces WRONG data), but the mechanic itself has no positive representation -- real, non-trivial modeling work (a delayed-timing dimension on top of the existing gift-condition machinery).

Stat-threshold ValidTgts$ qualifiers (po.description: A target's own printed power/toughness compared to a threshold, written directly into ValidTgts$ (Repel Calamity's own Creature.powerGE4,Creature.toughnessGE4 -- an OR of two stat checks; Sonar Strike's Creature.attacking,Creature.blocking,Creature.tapped is the same OR-of-qualifiers shape but for combat states). qualifierFlags' current design (an array of independently AND'd facts) doesn't cleanly support OR of qualifiers. Distinct from the already-implemented ConditionDefined$Targeted+ConditionPresent$ shape (a condition on an EARLIER target elsewhere in the chain, not the primary ValidTgts$ predicate).

Pawprint$ weighted/repeatable modal choi.description: Forge's Bloomburrow-specific 'choose up to N {P} worth of modes, may repeat' point-buy modal system (Season of the Burrow). SCHEMA's `combine` convention only supports a fixed choose-N-of-the-following shape, not a weighted/repeatable point-buy one. Individual mode effects still translate correctly; only the modal-choice wrapper itself is misrepresented (reads as a plain 'choose one').

Dig's look-then-selectively-reveal-to-ha.description: The current Dig handler only supports 'look at N, move the remainder to a stated DestinationZone$' -- it doesn't read Optional$/ChangeValid$/RestRandomOrder$/DestinationZone$-absent, all needed for Forge's very common 'look at the top N, you may reveal ONE matching card and put it into your hand, put the rest on the bottom in random order' idiom (Star Charter). Worth a real look since this shape recurs across many card types (not BLB-specific).

DB$ Play (cast from an alternate zone, o.description: A whole alternate-casting mechanic ("cast target instant/sorcery from your graveyard without paying its mana cost," Daring Waverider's own) plus its own replacement effect for where the spell goes afterward (ReplaceGraveyard$Exile). Zero handling -- genuinely new, moderately complex effect type, not a quick fix.

AlternativeDecider$ (a non-caster player.description: Dire Downdraft's own "target creature's owner puts it on the TOP OR BOTTOM of their library" -- AlternativeDecider$ names WHO makes the choice (here, the target's owner, not the caster), between DestinationAlternative$/LibraryPositionAlternative$-named outcomes. A genuinely new decision-maker/choice concept, entirely unread.

Count$PromisedGift.N.M (dynamic gift-con.description: A narrower cousin of the Condition class above: Dewdrop Cure's own SVar:X:Count$PromisedGift.3.2 means "3 if the gift was promised, else 2" -- swaps a NUMBER rather than gating an effect on/off (which the existing cond:gift_promised/gift_not_promised boolean flags already handle). Also covers the exclusive-or shape (Long River's Pull/Into the Flood Maw/Mind Spiral's own TargetMin$X/TargetMax$X where X = Count$PromisedGift.0.1 or .1.0 -- zeroing out one of two sibling effects depending on gift status, rendered as both happening unconditionally instead). Needs recognizing this specific Count$ shape and binding qty to a declared value via SCHEMA's :=/= label convention. Real modeling work, not a quick fix.

Defined$<sibling-effect-target> self-ref.description: Forge has a whole family of Defined$ values naming 'the object some OTHER effect in this same chain already resolved to' (Targeted, ParentTarget, TriggeredSourceLKICopy, Remembered, DelayTriggerRememberedLKI, ...) -- deriveOwner/coarseType have no general case for any of them, so they fall to defaults (owner:'me', thing:selfThing) that are only coincidentally correct when the referenced object happens to be self-controlled. Mind Spiral's own Defined$ParentTarget (referring to a SIBLING effect's own opponent-controlled target) is a concrete case that resolves wrong. Same broader gap as the already-documented Defined$Targeted entry -- would need threading the parent effect's own resolved owner/thing down into children, a broader signature change.

K:ETBReplacement (enters-as-a-copy / con.description: Forge's ETB replacement-effect keyword family (enters tapped conditionally, enters as a copy of another permanent, etc.) has no handler. Genuinely varied shapes, real feature work.

S:ReduceCost (cost reduction).description: No schema representation for cost reduction at all -- SCHEMA's `cost:` convention is for stating what something costs, not for a rule that lowers a printed cost under a condition. Recurring across several cards; now honestly surfaces as an unmapped S:ReduceCost entry (fixed earlier this session) rather than silently vanishing, but still unimplemented.

TargetsWithDifferentControllers$ (a mult.description: Run Away Together's own "choose two target creatures controlled by DIFFERENT players" -- a real, narrow targeting-restriction concept (relating two targets to each other) with no representation. Distinct from a single target's own qualifiers.

ConditionPresent$ Card.wasCast+!wasCastF.description: Otterball Antics's own "if this spell was cast from anywhere other than your hand" -- a real, narrow dynamic condition (checking THIS spell's own casting zone), distinct from the gift-promised/Threshold conditions already handled.

A:CopySpellAbility (copy target spell).description: Zero handling -- a genuinely new, moderately complex effect type (Kitsa, Otterball Elite's own "copy target instant or sorcery spell you control, may choose new targets"), plus its own self-referential IsPresent$ Card.powerGE3+Self activation-gate on the activated ability's cost (a third IsPresent$/ConditionPresent$ context beyond trigger-level and effect-level).

CopyPermanent (create a token copy of ta.description: DB$ CopyPermanent has no handler at all -- a genuinely new effect type (not a quick field/regex fix), but not big-rework/design-decision-needed either. Real backlog item, not blocking.

ValidSource$SpellAbility.YouCtrl on a Be.description: "Whenever this becomes the target of a spell or ability YOU CONTROL" -- the trigger node's owner field already means "whose occurrence" (self, correctly 'me'), but WHO CONTROLS THE TRIGGERING SOURCE is a different dimension with no home in the current trigger vocabulary. Narrower than the big Condition class -- a real, recurring gap (Flowerfoot Swordmaster, Mouse Trapper, Nettle Guard all hit it) worth a follow-up flag/field addition, not a full redesign.

Pure mana-only activated-ability cost (n.description: The generic activation-cost handler only recognizes a Cost$ containing T (tap) or Sac<> (sacrifice) -- a plain "{3}{W}: effect" cost with neither falls through completely uncosted (Warren Elder's own PumpAll). Would need a parallel cost-node path for the mana-only case.

AddReplacementEffect$ / non-Flying AddKe.description: Fixed this batch -- both now surface honestly as unmapped entries instead of vanishing silently. No node built yet (no schema role for either mechanic), but no longer a silent-drop bug.

Builder's Talent.note: See result.json -- ValidCard/ValidCards field-name split and missing .nonCreature qualifier both fixed 2026-09-04, all 3 Class levels now fully match. In blb-success.json.

Crumb and Get It.note: Fixed 2 real gaps 2026-09-04: Pump's KW$ field (a granted keyword, e.g. Indestructible, distinct from a P/T delta) was completely unhandled; ConditionPresent$...PromisedGift is now read as a narrow cond:gift_promised flag (distinct from the general unimplemented ConditionCheckSVar$ class). One precision gap remains open: the indestructible-grant node's `thing` is 'any' instead of 'creature' because Defined$Targeted ("the same creature the earlier Pump targeted") isn't resolved back to the sibling's target type -- would need threading target-type context between chained effects, a broader signature change not done here. Also confirmed the c_a_food_sac registries.json gap (flagged by the exam) is now fixed via this session's token-registry fill-out.

Coruscation Mage.note: See result.json -- .nonCreature qualifier fix (shared with Builder's Talent) plus a new Offspring cond:paid_at_cast marker both fixed 2026-09-04, full match. In blb-success.json.

Innkeeper's Talent.note: Spot-check batch 2. Confirmed PutCounter's owner (Creature.YouCtrl) already correct -- examining agent misread it, not a translator bug. Found and fixed a real silent-drop bug: the static handler's unmapped-fallback treated ANY AddKeyword$ value as "handled" (only Flying actually built a node), so AddKeyword$ Ward:1 vanished with zero trace. Fixed via a `handled` tracking flag. Also found AddReplacementEffect$ (a third grant-via-SVar field, distinct from AddTrigger$/AddStaticAbility$) was completely unwired -- fixed in forgeScript.ts, plus fixed a label bug where a missing Mode$ stringified to the literal text 'undefined'. Remaining open: Mode$ Phase's Phase$ field is unread (generic 'phase' trigger-type instead of 'beginning of combat'); Ward/replacement-effect mechanics themselves have no schema role yet (see known_gap_classes).

Eluge, the Shoreless Sea.note: Spot-check batch 2. No new bug class found -- confirms two already-known gaps: CharacteristicDefining$ (dynamic */* P/T, likely a smaller sibling of the sensor-role gap, not full Beza-tier) and a second Mode$ ReduceCost (same shape as Eddymurk Crab's, now at least surfaces honestly post this batch's static-handler fix). The nested SubAbility$->StaticAbilities$ 'remembered object gets a static ability' shape (granting the flooded land its Island type) also isn't followed -- not chased down further.

Eddymurk Crab.note: Spot-check batch 2. Found and fixed a real silent-drop bug: Mode$ ReduceCost (this card's own cost-reduction clause) matched none of the static handler's branches and vanished with no node AND no unmapped entry -- same fix as Innkeeper's Talent's AddKeyword bug (a `handled` flag + honest fallback), now surfaces as S:ReduceCost. Tap-as-effect (this card's own ETB tap-two-creatures) is now implemented (2026-09-04, Mouse Trapper's batch) -- confirmed via regenerated packet, this card's own Tap unmapped entry is gone. Two open gaps remain: S:ReduceCost (cost reduction has no schema representation) and K:ETBReplacement (enters-tapped-conditionally).

Jackdaw Savior.note: Spot-check batch 2. Found and fixed a systemic gap, not card-specific: ChangesZone/ChangesZoneAll with Origin$Battlefield->Destination$Graveyard (rule 700.4 'dies') fell through to the unreadable literal string 'changeszone' -- added an isDies check mirroring the existing isEnter one. Confirmed this also fixed Scavenger's Talent's base trigger in the same batch, so likely benefits several more untested BLB cards using 'whenever ~ dies'. Two narrower, card-specific qualifier gaps left open (multi-clause .YouCtrl/.withFlying, and a Beza-adjacent-but-narrower dynamic mana-value comparison on the return target).

Scavenger's Talent.note: Spot-check batch 2. Benefited from two shared-logic fixes made earlier in this same batch: the dies-trigger fix (base ability) and a new ChangeType$ fix (Level 3's non-targeted 'return a creature card' idiom via ChangeType$ Creature.YouOwn was wrongly read as 'this enchantment returns' -- selfMove's heuristic didn't know about ChangeType$ as a third way Forge names an external subject, alongside ValidTgts$/SacValid$). DB$ Mill (Level 2's effect) is now implemented (2026-09-04, mirrors SCHEMA's own mill-N worked example) -- card now shows zero unmapped entries.
